newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: AIB confirms Co-op interest but denies deal.
newsitem.headline: AIB confirms Co-op interest but denies deal.

text.p: Ireland's Allied Irish Banks confirmed reports on Sunday that it was interested in acquiring Britain's Co-operative Bank plc but denied that any deal had been reached.
A spokeswoman for the bank told Reuters: "Yes, it would be fair to say AIB, if the Co-op became available for sale, would be interested in acquiring it but we have no agreement with anybody."

She was responding to reports in Britain's Sunday Times which said that the Irish bank and British retailer J.Sainsbury might buy parts of Britain's Co-operative Wholesale society (CWS) if an entrepreneur's bid for the group was succesful.
According to the Sunday Times, Allied Irish Banks (AIB) would buy the highly succesful, CWS-owned Co-operative bank Plc for between 350 and 400 million pounds.
On Friday Andrew Regan's Guernsey-based investment trust Lanica LCA.L confirmed that a group it owns had planned to bid for CWS but was thwarted by legal moves.
The Sunday Times said AIB would acquire the bank if Galileo Group, a bidding vehicle, succeeded in breaking up the CWS organisation.
The Sunday Times said Sainsbury would join the bidding team with the aim of buying some of the larger CWS retail outlets. A Sainsbury spokeswoman declined to comment on what she called "speculation."

CWS, whose interests range from supermarkets to travel agents to funeral parlours and insurance, revealed a 10 million pound drop in pre-tax profits to 54.1 million pounds for the year to January 11 and took court action to fend off any bid.
